verdict.line: You lose if you let Volibear chain Q (Thundering Smash) into point-blank E (Sky Splitter) before level 6; you win if you survive to the mid-game stack snowball and he has no answer to Spirit Fire armor shred.

brief.thesis: Volibear has the lane advantage and the solo-kill edge because his all-in combo front-loads damage before Nasus has stacks or a reliable punish. The matchup evens out over 1725 games (51.1% Nasus) specifically because Nasus wins the long game: every Siphoning Strike (Q) last-hit stacks permanently while Volibear's kit offers no scaling answer to it.

theirWindow.when: Q (Thundering Smash) up, he's walking at you
theirWindow.what: He's about to engage with the gap-close stun. Don't stand still at minion-clear range; he will stun whoever he Attacks first and chain into W (Frenzied Maul) twice for the heal.

yourWindow.when: His Q (Thundering Smash) just went down
yourWindow.what: This is your trade window. Walk up and take a free Siphoning Strike (Q) or land Spirit Fire (E) on the wave, since he has no stun to open with for 10-12 seconds depending on rank.

powerCurve.note: Q stun lets him force early trades
W+E combo threatens an all-in kill
Fury of the Sands offsets his Stormbringer

Fully stacked Q splits any tower dive

start.why: The sustained-damage shield directly blunts his Q-into-W poke pattern and lets you hold farm priority instead of conceding it.

boots.why: Lower cooldowns on Wither and Spirit Fire matter more here than magic resist, since his early threat is physical on-hit, not burst magic.

core.why: Gives you the move-speed and on-hit damage to actually stick on him once Wither slows him, instead of just farming stacks passively.
The attack speed slow directly neutralizes his passive Attack Speed stacking (The Relentless Storm), which is how he scales fights.
Boosts your Soul Eater lifesteal healing against his sustained on-hit W (Frenzied Maul) poke.

situational.when: he is building into an on-hit or crit-heavy physical damage carry path
you are losing early trades to his W (Frenzied Maul) sustain and need the anti-heal and armor earlier than Frozen Heart
he builds tanky and you need the wave-clear slow from Spirit Fire plus on-hit zone control to keep sieging

runes.keystoneWhy: The sustain and move speed proc directly answer his all-in poke pattern (Q into W into W) by healing you back and letting you disengage before the second Frenzied Maul lands.

summoners.why: Ghost lets you close the gap after Wither slows him instead of eating his first-strike advantage, and Teleport is what actually lets this lane reach the stack-snowball stage OP.GG's data describes by letting you reset and keep farming instead of losing tempo to recalls.

playing.title: Farm with Q, not autos
playing.detail: OP.GG's own read on this lane is to keep distance while farming with Siphoning Strike (Q) rather than trading autos, since every secured last hit permanently raises your Q damage and he has nothing comparable.

playing.title: Respect his E at all times
playing.detail: Sky Splitter (E) has 1200 range and slows on hit, far outranging your entire kit except Wither. Never stand in open lane without a minion or terrain between you and his flat ground sightline.

playing.title: Wither before he commits Q
playing.detail: Wither (W) decelerates his Movement and Attack Speed over time; landing it the instant he starts walking in removes the speed boost that makes his Thundering Smash (Q) stun actually land.

playing.title: Trade only after his Q is down
playing.detail: His Q (Thundering Smash) is a 300-range dash-stun on a 12 to 10 second cooldown by rank; once it's spent he has no hard engage tool until it resets, so that's when you force Spirit Fire (E) trades.

playing.title: Zone with Spirit Fire on contested waves
playing.detail: Spirit Fire (E) reduces Armor for anyone standing in it; drop it on crashing waves so your autos and Q both spike in damage exactly when he's forced to contest the minions.

playing.title: Hold Fury of the Sands for forced fights
playing.detail: Your R only matters once it's up at level 6; until then you have zero answer to his all-in, so play around cooldowns and wave state rather than your own ultimate.

playing.title: Don't contest his Stormbringer landing
playing.detail: Volibear's R disables nearby towers temporarily on landing and grants him bonus Health; if he flashes it onto you at a tower, back off and let the tower trade rather than fighting him at full HP advantage.

brief.patchCaveat: The build order, rune pages, boots, and win-rate figures above come from measured OP.GG games on the current patch (16.19.1); the matchup reasoning, timing windows, and trade patterns are my own tactical read, not sourced data.

stats.opponentTip: It is important to avoid Volibear’s (E). Keep some distance while farming with [Q], and try to focus on growing and prolonging the laning phase.
